rows.selection_reason: No prior experiments exist, so the first step is to establish a baseline for multimodal performance. This experiment tests a basic multimodal setup with multiprofile, scgpt and imagenet_vit_l encoders, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of combining RNA and image modalities, which is central to the study, while keeping other components simple to assess foundational performance.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) has moderate accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation, isolating its impact on performance. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation (a key design choice) improves results compared to avgpool, balancing exploration and exploitation while maintaining consistency in other components.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation (config_001) outperforms transformer aggregation (config_002). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted while keeping avgpool aggregation and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (same as config_001) improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion type, a key design choice, while minimizing other changes to focus on potential gains from weighted fusion.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves high accuracy (0.7062). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping image encoder and fusion method same) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. It balances exploitation of the strong RNA encoder and fusion method with exploration of aggregation methods, which are critical for multimodal integration.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_008) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (while keeping other components constant) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current strong configuration with exploration of a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_008) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (a simpler, lower-dimensional representation) while keeping other components the same would maintain performance. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder complexity and isolates its impact on model performance, balancing exploitation of known strengths with exploration of design choices.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_008) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder and concat fusion (while keeping resnet50 and transformer aggregation) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder and fusion method, which are critical design choices with limited prior comparison. This balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of key variables.

The existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion yield high performance (config_008). This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_005) can match or exceed these results, isolating the RNA encoder's impact. It balances exploitation of known effective components (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) with exploration of a different RNA encoder, addressing uncertainty about its relative importance.

Existing evidence shows config_008 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping image encoder and fusion method consistent, helping determine if pca_n2000 could match scvi_n200's performance. This balances exploitation of resnet50/image strengths with exploration of RNA encoder alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, weighted fusion, and transformer aggregation (config_008) achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether switching to avgpool aggregation (while keeping other parameters the same) impacts performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation is critical, balancing exploitation of current high-performing components with exploration of key design choices.
